questionStem: A young rural worker is choosing between two paths. Choose the one you would advise, what it gives up, and why that cost comes with it.

options.text: Move to a city or industrial zone to work in a factory
Stay home and work in services, a craft village or farming with a side job

reasons.text: Factories do not let workers go back to visit their families.
The steadier factory work is in cities and industrial zones, so taking it means moving away from home.
Young workers care less about family once they have steady pay.
Factory pay is lower than income from farming.
Workers must pay for training before they can start.
This path means living in a city or industrial zone, where the source says living costs are high.
The work near home is services, a craft village or farming with a side job, where the source says income is often lower and irregular.
Living near family always costs more than living in a city.
Rural workers are not allowed to take factory jobs.

tradeOffs.text: Fewer chances to learn a trade or move up

reasons.text: Training is only for people who have already left their home area.
The source links staying in the home area with fewer chances to learn a trade or move up, so being close to home comes at that cost.
People who work near home do not need new skills.

challengeCandidates.label: TN1
challengeCandidates.whenShownForTeacher: When the chosen reason is not one the source supports
challengeCandidates.message: Read the paragraph about the path you chose again. Does it say this is why the drawback happens?

challengeCandidates.label: TN2
challengeCandidates.whenShownForTeacher: When the factory path is chosen
challengeCandidates.message: The source says many factory jobs need skills people have not been trained for. Does your choice take that into account?

challengeCandidates.label: TN3
challengeCandidates.whenShownForTeacher: When the stay-home path is chosen
challengeCandidates.message: The source says income on this path is often lower and irregular. Does your choice take that into account?

challengeCandidates.label: Fallback
challengeCandidates.whenShownForTeacher: When none of the above applies
challengeCandidates.message: Read the two paths again. What does your choice give up?

feedback.text: The source gives both paths gains and drawbacks. Neither is the right answer; what counts is seeing what your choice gives up and why that cost comes with it.
